final:
Working with film-crew → seedance-25-director.

**Session start:** this folder isn't a git repository and NOTES.md didn't exist, so I couldn't pull and there were no open items to report. I also had no shell this session, so nothing was committed or pushed. The package validator wasn't run either: I went through its checks by hand and found no failures. I created NOTES.md with today's entry.

**Plan:** 20 s ÷ 5 s average shot length = 4 shots. The camera moves from wide to medium to a close insert on the glass, then to her face. The camera never shakes: the tremor shows only in the water, the dust and the sound. All the planning files are in `film-crew/targmanchuhi-day6-tremor/`.

| # | s | Shot | Beat |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0–5 | Wide, 24mm, very slow push-in | The manager stands at the window (right of frame) and says: "There is no blasting. Not before the permits." |
| 2 | 5–10 | Medium, 50mm, still camera, on Narine | She turns to the village elders to translate. At 8 s a deep thud comes through the floor. She stops and looks down at the glass. |
| 3 | 10–14 | Close insert, 100mm macro | Rings spread on the water. At 12 s a second thud moves the glass a few millimetres and dust settles on the water. |
| 4 | 14–20 | Close-up, 85mm, slow push-in | Her eyes rise to the manager. Off screen he says "Trucks. On the highway." She does not translate and holds his gaze. |

**How the clips cut together:** all 4 shots come from one Seedance call, so the room, light and costumes match. On top of that:
- The camera always stays on the same side of the table.
- The manager is always on the right of frame and the elders on the left.
- The only light comes from the window on the right.
- The descriptions of the room and the characters are word-for-word the same in every prompt.
- Room hum and the low rumble carry the sound across each cut.

If one shot fails, each shot also has its own backup prompt in `08_storyboard.md`. Generate it alone and drop it in at the same second.

**Assumptions** (there are no story documents for the feature in the repo):
- The company is foreign and the manager speaks English. Seedance 2.5 can't voice Armenian dialogue, and Narine's silence is the beat anyway.
- The meeting is with two village elders.
- No casting photos were provided, so Narine's face will change between takes. Send them and I'll write the full prompt using them.

**Risks:**
- The model may merge shots 2 and 3, or frame shot 4 too wide. Check this on every take.
- Her lips part in shot 2, so the model may add a sound there. Remove it in post if it does.

## FINAL

**Settings:**
- Dreamina → Seedance 2.5 → Omni Reference
- Duration 20 s, ratio 16:9
- 720p for tests, 1080p for the keeper
- No uploads
- 3–4 takes

```text
No uploaded references; text-only generation.

A 20-second, four-shot dramatic scene in a monumental concrete meeting room of a mining company: while the foreign manager calmly denies any blasting, a deep tremor rises through the floor, and Narine, his interpreter, realises the secret blasting has begun; restrained, monumental, cold grey-blue large-format cinema with four natural shot switches.

Set: a double-height brutalist meeting room on the top floor of a mining company site office: raw board-marked concrete walls and ceiling, a long dark steel-and-oak table running across the frame, black leather chairs, a floor-to-ceiling window wall on the right side of the frame overlooking a grey terraced quarry and mountains dissolving in pale haze, a single water glass filled to the brim on the table in front of the seated woman, a closed grey folder beside it, no logos, no screens, no decorations.
Characters: Narine, an Armenian woman in her early thirties, dark brown hair pulled back in a low tight knot with a few loose strands at the temple, dark watchful eyes, natural no-makeup look, a charcoal wool turtleneck under a slate-grey tailored blazer, a white visitor badge on a dark grey lanyard, a thin steel wristwatch on her left wrist, no other jewelry. The manager, a broad-shouldered foreign man in his mid-fifties, close-cropped grey hair, clean-shaven, navy suit, white shirt open at the collar, no tie, hands relaxed in his trouser pockets. Two elderly village men in worn brown and dark green work jackets, one holding a flat cap on his knee.
Light: cold overcast daylight from the window wall on frame-right is the only light source; faces are lit from frame-right with a deep falloff into shadow on frame-left; desaturated grey-blue palette, concrete grey, no warm light; fine dust hangs visible in the window light; clean large-format digital image with fine grain.

[0-5s] Shot 1, wide shot at seated eye height, 24mm lens, an imperceptibly slow push-in. The long table runs across the frame; the manager stands by the window on frame-right, small against the huge concrete wall and the grey haze, half in silhouette; Narine sits at the middle of the far side of the table, turned three-quarters to camera, looking up and frame-right at him; the two village men sit at the left end of the table. The manager says in calm, measured English: {There is no blasting. Not before the permits.} Sound: low ventilation hum, faint wind against the glass, his voice slightly reverberant in the concrete room. ➖ no movement from anyone but the speaking manager, no extra people.
[5-10s] Shot 2, natural shot switch to a medium shot of Narine from the same side of the table, 50mm lens, locked camera; the full water glass soft in the lower-right foreground. She turns her head toward the village men on frame-left, draws a breath and parts her lips to translate. At 8 seconds a deep sub-bass thud rolls up through the floor; the water in the glass trembles and the glass ticks against the table. She stops, lips still slightly parted, and her eyes drop down to the glass. ➖ she makes no sound and says no words, the camera does not shake.
[10-14s] Shot 3, cut to an extreme close-up insert of the brimming water glass on the dark table, 100mm macro lens, locked camera at table height, the edge of her charcoal sleeve soft at the left edge of the frame. Concentric rings spread across the water surface. At 12 seconds a second, heavier thud: the rings break apart, the glass shivers a few millimetres across the table, and fine pale dust settles onto the water. Sound: low tremor rumble, a thin glassy hum, a faint creak from the window frame. ➖ the glass does not fall, break or spill, the camera does not shake.
[14-20s] Shot 4, cut to a close-up of Narine, 85mm lens, a very slow push-in, the cold window light from frame-right on her face. Her eyes rise slowly from the glass and turn frame-right toward the manager, who stays off-screen. Off-screen, the manager's voice, light and unhurried, almost amused: {Trucks. On the highway.} She does not translate. Her jaw tightens, she swallows once, and she stays perfectly still, holding his gaze; behind her, fine dust drifts down through the window light. Hold on her face to the end. ➖ no tears, no gasp, no head shake, she does not speak.

Global: the camera always stays on the same side of the table; the manager is always on frame-right, the village men always on frame-left, and Narine looks frame-right when she looks at the manager. One light source from frame-right in every shot; identical wardrobe and set in every shot. The camera never shakes; the tremor shows only in the water, the dust and the sound. Photorealistic humans retaining real fine pores and skin texture; restrained, internal acting. Sound: the room hum and wind continue under all four shots, the tremor rumble under shots 2 to 4; only the manager speaks, in English; Narine never speaks. Pure video, no subtitles, no background music, no on-screen text, no logos, no extra people, no slow motion.
```

**Timeline:**
- **0–5 s:** wide shot; the manager tells the lie.
- **5–10 s:** Narine starts to translate; the first thud stops her and her eyes drop to the glass.
- **10–14 s:** the glass; a second thud moves it and dust lands on the water.
- **14–20 s:** close-up of Narine; he lies again off screen; she stays silent.
